I am 58 years old and have farmed my land in Quzhou County for over 40 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this soil and this climate better than any book. Around here, the only sensible system is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plot — we call it "two crops a year." I have 5 mu of good flat land, and I am not going to gamble with cotton or vegetables. I need grain I can sell to the state purchasing station and keep some flour for my family.

This year I will stick with what has always worked. In late September I will rotary till the entire 5 mu and sow Jimai 22 wheat right after National Day. It is an improved variety that stands well against lodging and the local buyers recognize it. I will spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, then topdress urea at green-up and jointing — that comes to roughly 20 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from the cold, and three more times in spring at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. For pests, I will spray herbicide once after sowing and insecticide twice in the spring, so three applications in total. I expect about 1,050 kg per mu at harvest in early June.

The same day the wheat comes out, I will plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize. There is no time to plough — I will no-till plant straight into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed gives the yield. I will use about 1.2 packages per mu, put down compound fertilizer at planting, and add a side-dressing of urea when the plants reach the big trumpet stage. That is about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: at the trumpet stage and at flowering. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice, three applications total. I expect around 1,150 kg per mu by late September.

I do not see any reason to change this rotation. It feeds my family, it pays for the inputs, and it is what every experienced farmer in the village does.
